How this book matches your board exam. Research check: this book follows the CBSE Class 12 English Core syllabus for 2026–27 and the eight prose chapters of NCERT Flamingo: The Last Lesson, Lost Spring, Deep Water, The Rattrap, Indigo, Poets and Pancakes, The Interview and Going Places. In the 80-mark paper, Section C, Literature, carries 40 marks. Flamingo prose appears in: Q9 prose extract (6 marks), Q10 short answers (5 × 2 marks, 40–50 words, Flamingo prose and poetry) and Q12 long answer (5 marks, 120–150 words). Internal assessment (listening, speaking and project) carries 20 marks.

We do not reproduce the textbook passages. Read each chapter in your NCERT book; this guide gives summaries, themes, characters and practice in board style. Each unit ends with a 10-mark practice set. The marking points are our own, not the official CBSE marking scheme.

Unit 1 of 10: The Last Lesson (Alphonse Daudet)

Key ideas

  • Setting: a village school in Alsace, France, during the Franco-Prussian War (1870–71), when Alsace and Lorraine passed to Prussia.
  • Plot: Franz, a young boy, is late for school and fears a scolding because he has not learned participles. He finds the school unusually quiet; the teacher M. Hamel is dressed in his best clothes, and village elders, including old Hauser, sit at the back. M. Hamel announces that an order from Berlin means only German will be taught; this is his last French lesson.
  • Franz suddenly regrets wasting time; M. Hamel blames parents, pupils and himself for always putting off learning.
  • M. Hamel praises French as a beautiful, clear language and urges them to keep it, because holding on to one's language helps an enslaved people keep their identity.
  • At the end, overcome with emotion, he writes "Vive La France!" on the blackboard and dismisses the class.
  • Themes: linguistic chauvinism of the conquerors; love for one's language and nation; procrastination and regret.

Worked examples

Example 1: Why were the village elders in the classroom? Answer: to thank M. Hamel for his forty years of service and to show respect for the country that was no longer theirs.

10-mark practice set

  1. (2 marks) What was unusual about M. Hamel's dress and behaviour that day? Answer: he wore his best clothes — green coat, frilled shirt, black silk cap (1); he spoke kindly and did not scold Franz (1).
  2. (2 marks) What was the order from Berlin? Answer: only German was to be taught in the schools of Alsace and Lorraine (1); so this was the last French lesson (1).
  3. (1 mark) Who wrote The Last Lesson? Answer: Alphonse Daudet.
  4. (5 marks, long answer) "We should not put off learning." How does the story show this through Franz, the parents and M. Hamel? Answer: Franz had wasted time and now regretted not learning French (1); parents sent children to work on farms or mills to earn money (1); M. Hamel had sent pupils on errands and given holidays when he wanted (1); all realised too late that they could no longer learn French freely (1); conclusion — procrastination costs us what we value (1).

Common mistakes

  1. Mixing up Alsace and Berlin. 2. Saying M. Hamel was strict that day. 3. Missing the elders' reason. 4. Quoting lines inaccurately instead of paraphrasing. 5. No theme in long answers.

Quick recall

  1. Teacher? 2. Grammar topic Franz hadn't learned? 3. Region? 4. Last words on board? 5. Years of service?

Answers: 1) M. Hamel. 2) Participles. 3) Alsace. 4) "Vive La France!" 5) Forty.
